disposition: retain explicit orchestration with corrected coordination
invocation: explicit; retained disable-model-invocation requires provider verification

execution.recommended: single in-session dispatcher with bounded independent workers and isolated worktrees for concurrent code writes
execution.alternatives: sequential in-session implementation; authorized Herdr topology for visibility

changes.summary: Replace false atomic claim guarantees, direct API fallback, hardcoded main/focus and artifact-only completion with scoped dispatcher claims, base validation, evidence and explicit review state.

questions.question: Should one dispatcher own all claims and tracker updates?
questions.recommendation: Yes; workers return evidence rather than mutating shared ticket state.
questions.rationale: Shared self-assignment is not an atomic lock and hides child races.

questions.question: Does a sweep request alone authorize new Herdr topology?
questions.recommendation: Confirm topology separately unless already specified; allow sequential execution.
questions.rationale: Visibility and write isolation differ, and new workspaces consume shared resources.

validation: Static scenarios for shared identities, missing code prerequisites, untracked diffs, review-state dependencies, empty frontier, failed capacity and interruption.
limitations: No live agent, worktree, build or ticket workflow executed by candidate.
Provider invocation metadata and current Herdr CLI must be verified before promotion.
No discovered license; external dispatchers can still race.
